Region-level aggregate admissibility test (single threshold)

Source: R/aggregate.R
dn_aggregate.Rd

Tests whether a region holds more climatically admissible species than the null expects: the observed count of species whose coverage exceeds threshold against the Poisson-binomial expectation of the same count under each species' own null. One rule, both sides – applying a stricter criterion to the observed side than the null side guarantees a negative result regardless of the data.

Usage

dn_aggregate(obs, null_mean, null_sd, threshold)

Arguments

obs

length-n observed coverage values (one per species).

null_mean, null_sd

length-n per-species null moments.

threshold

coverage threshold.

Value

one-row data.frame: n_species, n_admissible_obs, expected, sd, dn_ses, p, enrichment, reliable.

Details

Only nulls whose marginals are genuinely counterfactual support this test (the environmental-shift null N2 or relocation null N3); the breadth-matched null reproduces the observed marginal by construction and has no power here.

Results with expected count < 5 are flagged reliable = FALSE: the normal approximation to the Poisson-binomial count is invalid there and the SES/enrichment are arithmetic, not evidence. Never report unreliable cells.

Examples

set.seed(1)
obs <- c(rbeta(300, 0.3, 3), rbeta(100, 4, 1.5))   # bimodal coverage
mu <- rbeta(400, 1, 3); sdv <- 0.05 + 0.1 * runif(400)
dn_aggregate(obs, mu, sdv, threshold = quantile(obs, 0.95))
#>   n_species n_admissible_obs expected        sd ses  p enrichment reliable
#> 1       400               20 1.162139 0.9684571  NA NA         NA    FALSE
